verdicts.note: Not resting on city votes: website opposes the 'capital gains income tax' as a stepping stone to a broader income tax and proposes a 0.1% sales-tax cut [S2]; 2026 interview pledges to cut taxes and oppose 'new fees and taxes' [S3]; plus the city levy vote [S7]. Repeated explicit statements on state taxes support -2 high even though the council votes alone would not.
Website and Herald-Republic interview both pledge cuts to 'wasteful' spending and administrative overhead [S2][S3]; NBC interview says he would have cut more on the council [S5].
Permitting reform to lower housing costs [S3] is pole_a; 'The Housing First model isn't working' [S2] is skepticism of the pole_b model. -1 medium is measured.

'Fully funding law enforcement', 'opposing reckless criminal justice rollbacks' [S2], 'fund the police as best we can' [S5] and treatment as a condition of housing aid (mandatory-treatment, pole_a) [S2].

Website plank 'Repeal the Climate Commitment Act' (verified in cached text) [S2] plus the interview pledge to reduce fuel taxes and energy regulations [S3]: two explicit statements matching pole_a's own wording.
Two years on the Yakima City Council and deputy mayor [S1][S2] against a candidate with no office: a modest proven record, so -1 rather than -2.

Quote verified in the cached NBC Right Now text: 'I believe there are 2 genders and science would not support their claim that there are expanding and infinite gender orientations' [S6], with his vote against the Pride proclamation. Gender/LGBTQ+ evidence, not schools; one statement plus one vote supports -2 at medium. No abortion evidence, which keeps it below high.

Website plank 'Empowering Parenthood' (verified): parents 'have the right to know what their children are being taught, what medical decisions are being made' [S2]. That is notification and record-access evidence, squarely parental-rights, not social. One campaign source, so medium.

2026 statement 'Reproductive rights are being gutted' [S1] and her 2022 candidacy as a Women's Reproductive Justice Party candidate pledging to 'fight like hell ... to protect abortion rights and safe abortion access' (verified) [S4]. Reproductive-policy evidence only; two statements four years apart support +2 medium.

The only evidence is one rhetorical clause in her statement, that Christian teachings are being hijacked 'to terrorize immigrants' [S1]. It expresses sympathy toward immigrants but states no position on enforcement, ICE cooperation or sanctuary policy. Direction is plausible, confidence low.

Statement says the environment and children's futures 'are being destroyed' [S1]; 2020 Herald-Republic lists her work with the Citizens' Climate Lobby [S5] (verified). An affiliation plus a current statement supports +1 medium, not more.
No government office [S1]; running under a No Kings label after several unsuccessful runs [S2][S4][S5]. Medium is appropriate because she frames no explicit renewal argument.

missing.basis: In the 2026-07-16 Herald-Republic interview he says Olympia's 'excessive taxes, regulations and mandates' stifle local schools and businesses, calls for 'local control over levies and spending priorities' and pledges to block state mandates 'that drain resources' from districts [S3]. This is about state fiscal mandates on local governments (levies, spending priorities), not curricula, notification or opt-outs, so it is local-control evidence under the 2026-10-08 addendum.
